Q: Dynamically rename a set of columns using Power Query A:

If you have the resulting column names you want, and the columns will always be the same (e.g., Name 2 will always be the second column), it seems like you could convert Source back to rows, then call Table.FromRows on List2:

let

    //list of original column names 
    List1= {"Name1","Name2","Name3","Name4"},

    //Create test table
    Source = Table.FromRows({{1231,1233,4121,5232},{3546,3426,1246,3464}} , List1),

    //list of new column names
    List2 = {"NewName 1","NewName 2","NewName 3","NewName 4"},

    Result = Table.FromRows(Table.ToRows(Source), List2)

in
    Result

Q: Using awk to split line with multiple string delimiters A: 
$ awk -F'[:,]' -v OFS=',' '{print $2,$6}' file
Jane,cat
John,dog
Jake,dog

As for why your attempt wasn't working, mainly it's because [ and ] in the context of a regular expression are the "bracket expression" delimiters and what goes inside that is a set of characters (which may be individual characters, ranges, lists, and/or classes) so when you wrote:

-F'['petOwner''petName''petType']'

that would set FS to the set of characters p, e, t, etc. not the set of strings petOwner, etc. The multiple internal 's are canceling each other out as you jump in/out of shell for no reason exactly as if you had written -F'[petOwnerpetNamepetType]' given there's no metacharacters in there that the shell would expand.

To set FS to a set of strings (actually regexps so watch out for metachars) would be:

-F'petOwner|petName|petType'

Q: Update column in table 1 with data from table 2 A:

Your query updates zero rows because it sets sb_bans.authid to the value it already has while joining on name instead of authid.

I'd join on the unique ID and set the column you want to update:

UPDATE sb_bans
JOIN sb_named ON sb_bans.authid = sb_named.authid
SET sb_bans.name = sb_named.name;

This uses multi-table UPDATE syntax. So you join the source table directly and set the target column from it.

Q: Identifying an event from a big Python list efficiently A:

We all know the naive solution: you need to loop over all the items in your list, like in this code

def just_loop_over(ls, k):
    found_zero = False
    events = []
    for i, x in enumerate(ls):
        if found_zero:
            if x > k:
                events.append(i)
                found_zero = False
        else:
            if x == 0:
                found_zero = True
    return events

So my idea is... loop over the list twice, but let Python builtins do their job - list.index() is far most efficient than anything we could ever write, and if we check for an item greater than K only after a zero, we can reasonably hope to skip a large number of items.

def use_builtins(ls, k):
    events = []
    zeros = []
    z = -1
    still_good = True
    while still_good:
        try:
            z = ls.index(0, z + 1)
            zeros.append(z)
        except:
            still_good = False
    zeros.append(len(ls))
    for z in range(len(zeros) - 1):
        for i, x in enumerate(ls[zeros[z] + 1:zeros[z + 1]], start = zeros[z] + 1):
                if x > k:
                    events.append(i)
                    break
    return events

I tried both functions on a random generated list of 10k values ranging from 0 to 999 (so I could expect about ten instances of zero), and the speed gain is about 2.5x, but I expect it should be greater than that on bigger lists.

Of course it depends on how many zeros are in the list and where they are, and where the first item following each zero and greater than K is. So for bigger Ks it will be a bit slower, for smaller Ks a bit faster.

As far as I know, if you want something more efficient, your only option is multiprocessing.

Q: What does the "__cplusplus" macro expand to? A:

Yes, it always does expand to numeric value and its meaning is the version of C++ standard that is being used. According to cppreference page, __cplusplus macro should expand to:

  • 199711L (until C++11),
  • 201103L (C++11),
  • 201402L (C++14),
  • 201703L (C++17),
  • 202002L (C++20)
  • 202302L (C++23)
  • 202603L (C++26)

The difference between #if and #ifdef directives is that #ifdef should be used to check whether given macro has been defined to allow a section of code to be compiled.

On the other hand #if (#else, #elif) directives can be used to check whether specified condition is met (just like typical if-condition).

Q: Error while deploying React App on Vercel A:

The Vercel log contains two different issues.

The first and most important one is:

git ls-remote --tags --heads ssh://git@github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-abi.git
Host key verification failed.
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

This means one of the project's dependencies is trying to install ethereumjs-abi from GitHub over SSH. Vercel's build environment cannot authenticate to that SSH dependency. This is a known issue with this dependency/setup and has been reported with the same Vercel error.

First check which package is bringing it in:

yarn why ethereumjs-abi

If it is directly in package.json as a GitHub/SSH dependency, replace it with a published npm version or an HTTPS Git dependency, for example:

"ethereumjs-abi": "^0.6.8"

Then remove the mixed package-manager lockfile. Your build is using Yarn, but the repository also contains package-lock.json.

Run:

rm -rf node_modules
rm -f package-lock.json
yarn install

Next, your second error is:

Error: Cannot find module '@babel/preset-react'

The log also says:

Disabled SWC as replacement for Babel because of custom Babel configuration ".babelrc"

So check .babelrc. If you don't actually need a custom Babel configuration, remove .babelrc and let Next.js use its default Babel/SWC setup.

If you do need .babelrc and it references @babel/preset-react, install it:

yarn add -D @babel/preset-react

For a normal Next.js custom Babel configuration, make sure you're using the Next.js preset, e.g.:

{
  "presets": ["next/babel"]
}

Finally, Vercel is also explicitly reporting that ESLint is missing:

ESLint must be installed in order to run during builds

Install it with:

yarn add -D eslint

Then test exactly what Vercel will run:

yarn install
yarn build

Only after that succeeds, commit package.json and yarn.lock and push again.

So the important point is that this isn't really a Vercel/React problem. Your local build works because your local environment already has the required dependencies and SSH/Git configuration. Vercel performs a clean dependency installation and exposes the undeclared/SSH dependency.

There is also a Stack Overflow question with the same ethereumjs-abi / Host key verification failed error, where switching the dependency away from GitHub SSH to HTTPS resolved the deployment issue.

For an additional deployment guide, this article may also be useful: https://www.blogs-world.in/blog/how-to-deploy-a-react-app-on-vercel/

References:

  • Vercel discussion showing the same ethereumjs-abi SSH/host-key failure

  • Next.js documentation regarding custom Babel configuration
